name: Gopīnātha Paṭṭanāyaka
add: Nandgram Dham: the second of the five sons of Bhavānanda Rāya, younger brother of Rāmānanda Rāya and elder brother of Vāṇīnātha; one of the five sons the Lord called the five Pāṇḍavas (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.132–133). «Paṭṭanāyaka» is an inherited Oḍiyā title of office, not a personal name. His deliverance is told in Antya-līlā 9.

name: Govinda dāsa Kavirāja
add: Nandgram Dham: family home Śrīkhaṇḍa, near Kāṭoyā (Bardhamān); traditional dates c. 1535 – c. 1613 (secondary sources; the Caitanya-caritāmṛta gives none). Major works: Saṅgīta-mādhava and Gītāmṛta.

name: Govinda Datta
add: Nandgram Dham: the twenty-sixth branch of the Caitanya tree, after Govindānanda (25th); principal singer in the Lord's own kīrtana party, and one of the five responding singers in the first of the four kīrtana parties at the Purī Ratha-yātrā. At his śrīpāṭa in Sukhacara he installed Śrī Śrī Nitāi-Gaurāṅga.

name: Govinda Ghoṣa
add: Nandgram Dham: also called Ghoṣa Ṭhākura. At the Ratha-yātrā he led his own kīrtana party, with his brothers Mādhava and Vāsudeva as responding singers.

name: Śrī Haridāsa Ṭhākura
add: Nandgram Dham: left this world on Ananta Caturdaśī (year unclear). His 300,000 names a day are about 175 rounds of japa. The Caitanya-caritāmṛta and the Caitanya-bhāgavata name no guru for him; later biographies (Advaita-prakāśa, Prema-vilāsa) name Advaita Ācārya. The Lord visited him every day in Purī.

name: Hemalatā Devī
add: Nandgram Dham: her mother was Īśvarī (also called Draupadī), Śrīnivāsa's first wife (another source: his second wife Gaurāṅga-priyā, also called Padmāvatī); sisters Kṛṣṇa-priyā and Kāñcana (Yamunā); half-brother Gati-govinda, son of the second wife. A dīkṣā guru of men and women, compared in the tradition to Jāhnavā Devī; her best-known disciple was Yadunandana dāsa, author of the Karṇānanda. She drove the schismatic Rūpa Kavirāja out of the Vaiṣṇava community.

name: Īśāna Ṭhākura
add: Nandgram Dham: the fifty-eighth branch of the Caitanya tree (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.110). He held the infant Nimāi, met His every childish demand, and was called «father» by Him. His birth and death dates are not recorded; he lived to a very great age.

name: Śrī Īśvara Purī
add: Nandgram Dham: his name before sannyāsa is not recorded. He wrote the Śrī Kṛṣṇa-līlāmṛta; his chief disciples Kāśīśvara and Govinda were later sent to serve Śrī Caitanya.

name: Jagadānanda Paṇḍita (Jagadānanda-Caitanya-Sakhā)
add: Nandgram Dham: also called Jagā. His birthplace is disputed: translations of his own book name either Kumārahaṭṭa (Hālisahar) or Kāñcanapallī near Navadvīpa. Author of the Prema-vivarta, twenty chapters in Bengali of pastimes and teaching. His closest companions in Purī: Svarūpa Dāmodara, Govinda and Gadādhara Paṇḍita. His disappearance is not recorded in any source.

name: Jagadīśa Paṇḍita
add: Nandgram Dham: the thirty-first branch of the Caitanya tree and the fifteenth of Nityānanda's; brought the Deities of Jagannātha and Gaura-Gopāla from Purī to Bengal. Some ISKCON communities keep his disappearance on the same day as Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī's.

name: Śrī Jagannātha dās Bābājī
add: Nandgram Dham: born c. 1750 or c. 1800 (sources disagree), in the Tangail subdivision of Mymensingh. Line: Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa → Uddhava dāsa Bābājī → Madhusūdana dāsa Bābājī → Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī; his principal disciple in this line was Bhāgavata dāsa Bābājī, the guru of Gaura Kiśora dāsa Bābājī. He left this world after 1897, on the new moon of Phālguna, a fortnight before Gaura Pūrṇimā; his age is given as 135 to 147. His samādhi stands on the Gaṅgā at Navadvīpa.

name: Jagannātha Tīrtha
add: Nandgram Dham: the 78th branch of the Caitanya tree (Ādi 10.114); one of the nine principal sannyāsī associates of the Lord (Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī's Anubhāṣya). His birth, death, guru and works are not recorded. Not the later Jagannātha Tīrtha, 23rd pontiff of the Vyāsarāja Maṭha.

name: Śrīmatī Jāhnavā Mātā
add: Nandgram Dham: her father Sūryadāsa Sarakhela was accountant to the ruler of Gauḍa. After 1534 she was a dīkṣā guru and the acknowledged head of the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas; Narottama, Śrīnivāsa and Śyāmānanda, initiated by others, took her as śikṣā guru. Her own dīkṣā guru is not named in any surviving source.

name: Śrī Jayadeva Gosvāmī
add: Nandgram Dham: his birthplace Kenduli (Kendubilva) is claimed both by Birbhum (West Bengal) and by Kenduli Sasan near Purī (Odisha); his mother is called Vāmādevī or Rāmādevī; Padmāvatī was a temple dancer given to him by Lord Jagannātha's arrangement. The Gīta-govinda has twelve cantos. Where he left this world is told differently: Kendubilva, Purī or Vṛndāvana.

name: Śrī Jayadharma
add: Nandgram Dham: known outside the Gauḍīya lists as Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha (also Jayadhvaja Tīrtha), author of the Padaratnāvalī (Bhakti-ratnāvalī, «Vijayadhvajīyam»), a major Dvaita commentary on the Bhāgavatam. Pontiff of the Pejawar Maṭha, usually dated 1381–1410 (other sources: until c. 1448–1450). The Pejawar records name Mahendra Tīrtha as his guru, the Gauḍīya list Rājendra Tīrtha. Disciples: Viṣṇu Purī (devotional tradition); his successor at Pejawar was Uttama Tīrtha.
